themes.consensus_view: Banks broadly agree that spending on AI infrastructure keeps rising and is now the main engine of big-tech earnings and new borrowing, though some warn the heavy spending is starting to squeeze cash flow and slow profit growth.

facts_agreed.claim: AI infrastructure demand and capex remain strong, supporting upside to earnings and continued heavy debt issuance.
evidence_quotes: We see upside to earnings estimates across most sub-sectors
we believe consensus 2027 capex estimates are once again too conservative.
We remain supportive of robust issuance across European and US credit markets

facts_agreed.claim: Orbital, space-based compute is emerging as a scalable new source of AI infrastructure capacity.
evidence_quotes: SPCX represents a unique opportunity from an AI and compute capacity perspective.
orbital compute could extend this advantage as SpaceX combines Starship, satellite manufacturing, space-based solar power

facts_contested.claim: net effect of AI capex on earnings and equity valuations
facts_contested.for_evidence: We see upside to earnings estimates across most sub-sectors
facts_contested.against_evidence: earnings per share growth is likely to slow, influencing equity valuations

themes.consensus_view: Banks broadly agree that SpaceX's Starship rocket, thanks to its reusability and large payload, will sharply cut the cost of reaching orbit and open up a fast-growing space economy, with market-size and revenue forecasts running into the trillions over the next decade-plus.

facts_agreed.claim: Starship's full reusability and large payload put it on track to slash launch costs and unlock the broader space economy.
evidence_quotes: SPCX is at the beginning of a particularly catalyst-rich 2-3 years
Starship, with 5x+ the max payload of Falcon 9 and full-reusability... has a realistic opportunity to significantly cut launch costs

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple desks reference Starship's launch-cost reduction, reusability, and economic potential as the core enabler of the space economy.

themes.consensus_view: Banks split on chip stocks: Goldman sees more room to run as chip demand normalizes, while The Market Ear warns the sector has broken down and big investors are aggressively selling.

facts_contested.for_evidence: Expect broad upside but run in stocks raises the bar
facts_contested.against_evidence: Semiconductor stocks have now closed below their 20-day moving average for 2 consecutive days

themes.consensus_view: Deutsche Bank, Goldman Sachs, and JPMorgan all reference the Strait of Hormuz supply-chain situation tied to the Iran conflict, but none stakes a clear directional view, with framings running from ongoing stress and disruption to stabilization and normalization.

facts_agreed.claim: Three banks flag the Strait of Hormuz supply-chain situation, linked to the Iran conflict energy shock, as a live macro topic this window without staking a primary directional call.
evidence_quotes: Strait of Hormuz supply chain normalization
Strait of Hormuz supply chain disruptions

themes.consensus_view: Several desks reference corporate share buybacks as an active market factor this window — from blackout-period timing to a boost for earnings per share — but none stakes a clear directional call.

facts_agreed.claim: Multiple banks flag corporate share buybacks as an active influence this window, spanning new authorizations, blackout-period timing, and a tailwind to earnings per share.

themes.consensus_view: Only JPMorgan stakes a directional view, arguing the shift of investor money out of big Tech and into the rest of the market has already begun and may run further.

facts_agreed.claim: The rotation of investors out of Tech into the broader market has already started, with room for it to continue.
evidence_quotes: The market broadening appears to have already begun, with the risk of further moves.

themes.consensus_view: Several desks flag that hedge funds and active managers are trimming crowded bets, especially in momentum stocks (recent winners) and semiconductors, but nobody has staked out a directional view on where prices go from here.

facts_agreed.claim: Three desks flag investors pulling back from crowded momentum-factor and active-manager positions as a live current-market dynamic.

themes.consensus_view: Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, and RBC all reference the Cursor acquisition and its integration as a live corporate development, but none has taken a clear bullish or bearish position on it.

facts_agreed.claim: Three banks flag the Cursor acquisition and its integration as a current corporate development worth tracking this window.
